commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Edea, Possessed Sorceress ({2}{U}{B}{R} 2/5 legendary Human Warlock, ward {2}; Final Fantasy Commander fic, released 2025-12-05; commander-legal, not a Game Changer, no project exception). At the beginning of combat on our turn she steals target opponent's creature until end of turn, untaps it and gives it haste. Whenever a creature we control but don't own dies, it returns under its owner's control and we draw. Plan: steal every combat (extra combats: Full Throttle, Karlach, Aggravated Assault, Combat Celebrant), sacrifice the stolen creature to free outlets for Edea's draw plus aristocrat payoffs (Grim Haruspex, Pitiless Plunderer, Mayhem Devil, Grave Pact), keep the best ones (Thassa, Kaya's Ghostform, Impostor Syndrome, Saw in Half), multiply her (Roaming Throne, Strionic Resonator, Irma, Gogo, Sakashima, Spark Double, Hall of Echoes), and finish with mass theft (Insurrection, Mass Mutiny, Mob Rule).
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Power Bracket 4 (Optimized). Game Changers: 3 in baseline and candidate (Ancient Tomb, Demonic Tutor, Fierce Guardianship). Commander Spellbook find-my-combos: 0 included combos for both lists (almost-included 126 -> 167). No infinite is claimed; repeated Aggravated Assault activations need {3}{R}{R} each and are finite.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Commander-first to Edea's Oracle: Aggravated Assault and Combat Celebrant add combats (each a theft); Hall of Echoes doubles Edea; Kaya's Ghostform turns her theft permanent while she still draws; Geyadrone Dihada adds theft density in the main phase. Distinctness (nonbasic names shared with the most similar approved Grixis decks, baseline -> candidate): Marchesa, the Black Rose 50 -> 49; Missy 46 -> 46; Wick, the Whorled Mind 45 -> 45; Tresserhorns 44 -> 43; Thraximundar 43 -> 43; Lord Xander 41 -> 43; Don Andres (the closest theft deck) 39 -> 38. Disclosed honestly: the shared core is the mana base, rocks, free interaction and generic outlets; separation is commander-first: every add multiplies or protects Edea's own two triggers (combat theft and death draw). Owner-removed or rejected classes (Garland, Beast, Coercive Recruiter, Morbid Opportunist, Dictate, Reliquary Tower and the conditional duals; Marchesa, Domineering Will, Nasty End, Cunning Rhetoric, Conjurer's Closet, Chameleon/Quantum Misalignment/Sakashima-type clones, Helm of Possession, extra outlets, Rhystic Study, Vampiric Tutor, Force of Will, The One Ring, Breath of Fury) are not re-added. Cuts of owner-retained cards are flagged: Evereth was explicitly challenged and kept by the owner, so a keep-Evereth four-swap is staged.

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps:
All 99 library cards were reviewed by quantity (93 library rows; Island, Mountain and Swamp 3x each, everything else 1x).
Roles:
- 35 lands, including Ancient Tomb, Arcane Lighthouse, Phyrexian Tower, Otawara and High Market (cut for Hall of Echoes).
- Rocks: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone, three Talismans.
- Extra combats: Full Throttle, Karlach; Aggravated Assault and Combat Celebrant are new.
- Multipliers: Roaming Throne, Strionic Resonator, Irma, Gogo, Sakashima of a Thousand Faces, Spark Double; Hall of Echoes is new.
- Theft: Captivating Crew, Mass Mutiny, Insurrection, Mob Rule, Dominus of Fealty, Don Andres, Rakdos, Seize the Spotlight and Zara (both cut); Geyadrone Dihada is new.
- Retention: Thassa, Impostor Syndrome, Saw in Half, Nightmare Shepherd, Chaos Shrine's Black Crystal; Kaya's Ghostform is new.
- Outlets: Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Goblin Bombardment, Viscera Seer, Warren Soultrader, Illuminor Szeras, Phyrexian Tower; Evereth, Ayara and High Market are cut. Spell outlets: Village Rites, Deadly Dispute, Corrupted Conviction, Diabolic Intent, Victimize.
- Payoffs: Grim Haruspex, Pitiless Plunderer, Mayhem Devil, Grave Pact, Braids, Skullclamp, Kethek, Industrial Advancement, Disciple of Bolas.
- Interaction: Fierce Guardianship, Mana Drain, Swan Song, Arcane Denial, Deflecting Swat, Deadly Rollick, Chaos Warp, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Vandalblast, Toxic Deluge, Blasphemous Act, Lightning Greaves.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: Baseline and candidate: 35 lands (9 basics), 6 rocks plus Ancient Tomb; coloured sources U19 B19 R18, unchanged (Hall of Echoes replaces the colourless High Market). Average nonland MV 3.203 -> 3.156; creatures 24 -> 22; instants and sorceries 24 -> 23; MV of cuts 14 vs adds 11. Exact multivariate-hypergeometric DP (mechanics test, on the play, a conservative model counting every rock as one mana): turns 3-7 P(lands >= turn) 0.6811/0.4984/0.3342/0.2069/0.1191 and P(Edea castable with U, B and R) 0.0456/0.2304/0.4878/0.588/0.6772, identical for baseline and candidate; on the draw Edea is castable by turn 5/6 at 0.588/0.6772.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Stack: Fierce Guardianship, Mana Drain, Swan Song, Arcane Denial, Deflecting Swat. Removal: Deadly Rollick, Chaos Warp, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Vandalblast. Wipes: Toxic Deluge, Blasphemous Act. Protection: ward {2}, Lightning Greaves, Otawara. Arcane Lighthouse beats hexproof/shroud on the theft target. Weak points: a five-mana commander that must survive to combat; tables with no good creatures (Dihada's +1 and Hall still have uses); graveyard exile stops Ghostform; enchantment removal hits Assault; Hall becomes a creature when it copies.

material_candidates.source: EDHREC Edea general 311/4819, upgraded 29/456, optimized 11/72; live Scryfall batch
material_candidates.role: {2}{R} enchantment: {3}{R}{R}: untap all creatures you control; after this main phase there is an additional combat phase followed by an additional main phase; sorcery speed, repeatable.
material_candidates.incumbent_opportunity_cost: Loses Evereth, a 3-MV flier and sorcery-speed outlet whose death trigger drains each opponent for its power. FLAG: the owner explicitly challenged Evereth on 2026-10-14 and kept it as a real baseline card; a four-swap list keeping Evereth is staged.
material_candidates.commander_synergy: Each extra combat has its own beginning of combat step (500.8, 506.1), so every activation is one more Edea theft and untaps the creatures we stole earlier. The extra main phase lets us activate again (ruling 2004-10-04): each {3}{R}{R} is one more steal. Pass C itself names Aggravated Assault as an Edea extra-combat source.
material_candidates.adversarial_downside: Five mana per activation; does nothing on the turn it is cast without more mana; enchantment removal answers it. Commander Spellbook lists opponent-dependent near-combos (a stolen Ancient Copper Dragon or Reaver Cleaver), which are disclosed and NOT claimed as infinite.
material_candidates.reason: A repeatable source of Edea's own trigger that converts late-game mana into theft; Evereth is a generic outlet in a deck with seven other free, repeatable outlets.

material_candidates.source: EDHREC Edea general 359/4819, upgraded 34/456, optimized 4/72; live Scryfall batch
material_candidates.role: {B} Aura for a creature or planeswalker you control: when it dies or is exiled, return that card to the battlefield under your control.
material_candidates.incumbent_opportunity_cost: Loses Zara, a 5-MV flier whose attack trigger puts a creature from the defending player's hand onto the battlefield attacking; that creature goes back to hand at end step.
material_candidates.commander_synergy: Put on a stolen creature, then sacrifice it: Ghostform and Edea trigger together, we order Ghostform to resolve first (603.3b) and the card comes back under OUR control as a new object (400.7). Edea's trigger then does as much as it can (609.3): no return, but we still draw. Unlike Marchesa, which the owner rejected because it is a delayed return, Ghostform is not delayed. It answers the Pass C warning that sacrificing a stolen creature hands it back to its owner.
material_candidates.adversarial_downside: One use; if an opponent regains control of the creature first, the Aura goes to the graveyard; graveyard exile in response stops the return.
material_candidates.reason: Turns Edea's temporary theft into permanent theft for one mana and still draws; Zara's stolen creature only borrows a card from a hand and returns it to hand.

low_swap_heightened_audit.alternate_cuts_for_prior_holds: Pass C's Conjurer's Closet tests (vs Impostor Syndrome, Industrial Advancement and Irma) were run as bounded finite tests; all three are staged as complete six-swap 100s and rejected (Pass C KEEP and the owner's Closet rejection respected). Celebrant vs Grim Haruspex (Pass C DEFER) was measured; Haruspex is kept and Celebrant replaces Seize the Spotlight instead. The owner-kept Evereth has a staged keep-Evereth four-swap.
low_swap_heightened_audit.strongest_argument_against_baseline: Edea's value is counted in combats and in deaths of stolen creatures, yet the baseline spent five slots on three redundant generic outlets (the owner wrote that no outlet shortage remains), a 5-MV theft that returns to hand, and a one-shot whose mode the opponents choose. It also had no way to keep a sacrificed stolen creature.
low_swap_heightened_audit.evidence_based_answer: Five swaps: two repeatable extra-combat sources (Aggravated Assault, Combat Celebrant), an Edea copy in a land slot (Hall of Echoes), permanent theft that still draws (Kaya's Ghostform), and main-phase theft density (Geyadrone Dihada). Coloured sources and mana unchanged; outlet density cost disclosed (10 -> 7). Spellbook: 0 included combos before and after.

final_candidate.deckwide_reconciliation: Commander first, then lines alphabetically; 3x Island, 3x Mountain, 3x Swamp, everything else 1x. Five substitutions against the canonical source. 35 lands; 100 physical cards verified by quantity (99 library + 1 commander).

open_ended_optimization_audit.remaining_99_review: The five-swap floor was reached with five swaps that each stand on their own; the floor was not used as a target and no sixth swap cleared the bar. Every remaining incumbent was re-read against the candidate pool: eight post-floor challenges were recorded on Edea-specific grounds, and three Pass C six-swap packages (Conjurer's Closet over Irma, Impostor Syndrome or Industrial Advancement) are staged as complete 100s.

post_floor_challenges.tradeoff: Bounded 32-cell grid: Irma 216 steal triggers vs Closet 120; Closet keeps 48 vs 16 creatures, but Thassa already keeps one in half the cells. Irma wins on steals in 28/32 cells.
8-cell grid: Impostor's permanent token copies tie or beat Closet's one keep in 6 cells and beat it in 4; Pass C's requested test.
Exact hypergeometric: Advancement hits a creature 0.7308 at MV5 (80 cards, 18 creatures) on top of Edea's draw; Closet only repeats Thassa's keep.
Lithoform copies one trigger per turn for {2}; Kethek turns every stolen body into a permanent creature of ours each end step. The owner preferred theft and combats over multipliers.
Greaves re-equips for free, so it can protect Edea or a newly kept creature at no mana cost; Boots costs {1} every time it moves.

open_ended_optimization_audit.quality_based_stop_reason: Stopped at five. Each remaining weak-looking slot beats its best challenger on Edea-specific grounds: Irma, Impostor Syndrome and Industrial Advancement each beat Conjurer's Closet in the bounded Pass C tests (and the owner rejected Closet); Kethek beats another multiplier; Greaves, Victimize, Mob Rule and Disciple beat generic challengers.
